# UKIP 2010 Manifesto Summary

The UK Independence Party's 2010 manifesto centres on one fundamental premise: Britain must withdraw from the European Union to restore national sovereignty, prosperity, and democratic self-governance. UKIP positions itself as the only party representing the majority of British people who, they argue, consistently favour EU withdrawal but have been denied any referendum by the "LibLabCon consensus."

## Core Argument: EU Withdrawal

UKIP contends that EU membership costs Britain up to £120 billion annually through direct contributions, bureaucratic red tape, and lost economic opportunities. They reject claims that EU membership protects British trade and jobs, arguing instead that as the EU's largest single trading partner, Britain would maintain favourable trade relationships outside the union while escaping crippling over-regulation. The party advocates replacing EU membership with a Swiss-style free trade agreement.

## Economic Vision

UKIP proposes radical tax simplification, including introducing a 31% flat tax starting at an £11,500 threshold, removing minimum wage earners from taxation entirely. They advocate scrapping 120,000 EU directives, abolishing inheritance tax, and replacing VAT with a Local Sales Tax. The party promises to reduce the public sector to 1997 levels, creating manufacturing jobs through major investment programmes in defence, nuclear power, flood defences, transport, and prisons.

## Immigration

Central to UKIP's platform is regaining border control through EU withdrawal. They propose an immediate five-year immigration freeze, aspiring to limit future immigration to 50,000 annually. All EU citizens arriving after 2004 would lose preferential status, asylum seekers would be held in secure centres, and there would be no amnesty for illegal immigrants. UKIP opposes multiculturalism, promoting instead "uniculturalism" to create a single British identity.

## Constitutional Reform

UKIP advocates binding national and local referenda, an element of proportional representation, directly elected local boards for police, health, and education, and the abolition of regional government. They propose replacing devolved assemblies with Westminster MPs meeting separately for devolved business.

## Defence and Foreign Policy

The party promises a 40% increase in defence spending, expanding the Army by 25%, restoring the Royal Navy, and maintaining an independent nuclear deterrent. They would strengthen NATO commitments while withdrawing from EU operations and establish a Commonwealth Free Trade Area to revitalise trade relationships with 53 Commonwealth nations.

## Social Policy

UKIP proposes a non-means-tested Citizen's Pension of £130 weekly, simplified welfare through a Basic Cash Benefit system, School Vouchers for parental choice, and Health Credit Vouchers enabling NHS opt-out. They advocate grammar school expansion, abolishing the Human Rights Act, doubling prison places, and introducing "three strikes" sentencing.

## Environment

UKIP takes a sceptical stance on man-made climate change, calling for nuclear power to provide 50% of electricity, supporting coal extraction, opposing most wind farms, repealing the Climate Change Act, and withdrawing from EU carbon trading schemes.

The manifesto presents withdrawal from the EU as the essential precondition for implementing all other policies, framing it as a restoration of British democracy, sovereignty, and common sense.
